lifecycle.origin: Created 2026-08-18 by KERNEL_BUILDER-20260818-130753. MT-137's progress notes already flagged that tests asserting deleted PostgreSQL DDL constants 'cannot survive the pivot and need their own microtask' (naming process_ledger_tests.rs, process_ledger_reclaim_tests.rs, focus_audit_tests.rs, hbr_e2e_smoke_test.rs). A census on 2026-08-18 measured the true surface: ~190 files under src/backend/handshake_core/tests/ carry sqlx usage, PostgreSQL DSNs, psql spawns, apply_migration() calls, or PG language — the whole backend test tree was authored against the deleted PostgreSQL storage layer. The Operator directive forbids PostgreSQL/SQLite dependency and language in tests and checks.

field_evidence_disclosure_2026_09_04.note: Disclosure only. No MT-141 requirement, acceptance criterion, proof target, or status is changed by this entry. Found while repairing branch CI under MT-147, which is forbidden to touch this tree.
field_evidence_disclosure_2026_09_04.finding: src/backend/handshake_core/tests/** does not compile at all. Cargo.toml declares tempfile = "3", which resolves to 3.27.0, and TempDir::from_path no longer exists in that version. tests/atelier_surreal_support/mod.rs:124 still calls tempfile::TempDir::from_path(data_dir), and lines 41 and 159 still call the deprecated into_path().
field_evidence_disclosure_2026_09_04.observed_verbatim: error[E0599]: no associated function or constant named `from_path` found for struct `TempDir` in the current scope --> tests/atelier_surreal_support/mod.rs:124:49 | 124 | Self::open_directory(tempfile::TempDir::from_path(data_dir)).await | ^^^^^^^^^ associated function or constant not found in `TempDir`. Followed by: error: could not compile `handshake_core` (test "atelier_command_corpus_tests") due to 1 previous error.
field_evidence_disclosure_2026_09_04.evidence: GitHub Actions run 33818193204, job cross-platform-build (job id 100854799834), which ran cargo check --all-targets --all-features on ubuntu-latest at product 8e0daf25.
field_evidence_disclosure_2026_09_04.platform_independence: This is a dependency API change, not a platform difference, so the same break applies on Windows. It is why cargo check --all-targets has not been passing anywhere.
field_evidence_disclosure_2026_09_04.effect_on_mt_147: The MT-147 cross-platform job was rescoped to --lib --bins plus a --lib --no-run test compile, so it proves the crate surface MT-118 and MT-144 depend on without reporting this defect as its own. The rescope is recorded in commit 817fca6f.
field_evidence_disclosure_2026_09_04.owner_question: MT-141 owns tests/**. This needs either a tempfile pin or a migration to TempDir::new_in plus keep(), and it should be decided inside MT-141 rather than patched from an adjacent microtask.
field_evidence_disclosure_2026_09_04.suggested_migration: tempfile 3.27 removed TempDir::from_path and deprecated TempDir::into_path in favour of keep(). The helper needs either a pin to a tempfile version that still has from_path, or a rewrite of open_existing that does not try to wrap an already-existing directory in a TempDir at all. The second is likely correct: open_existing takes ownership of a caller-supplied path for a close-and-reopen durability proof, which is not what TempDir is for.

scope.summary: Port src/backend/handshake_core/tests/ off sqlx/PostgreSQL onto the embedded SurrealDB store. These tests compile against the handshake_core lib, so this MT is implementable only after MT-136/137/138 make the lib compile cleanly. Patterns to follow: unit-adjacent storage tests use SurrealStorage opened at a temporary HANDSHAKE_DATA_DIR (see tests/surreal_test_store_support/ and storage/surreal/test_inspector.rs behind the surreal-test-support feature); API-level tests exercise the product HTTP surface; migration-corpus assertions (apply_migration, DDL-constant asserts) are retired with the corpus per MT-139's recorded SEVER decision and replaced by the schema.surql coverage proof. Test-only isolation comes from per-run data directories, never from schemas or shared clusters. No assertion may be weakened or deleted to make a file compile; each file's proof intent is preserved at equivalent strength or the file's owning behavior is recorded as no-longer-existing with the superseding proof named.

acceptance_criteria.text: No file under src/backend/handshake_core/tests/ references sqlx, PostgreSQL, psql, PG DSN env vars, SQLite, or PL/pgSQL language, except deliberate forbidden-technology tripwires whose purpose is detection.
Every retained test compiles and its proof intent is preserved at equivalent strength against the embedded store; every retired test names the superseding proof or the removed behavior it covered.
Durability-class tests (process ledger, session checkpoint, CRDT persistence, EventLedger) prove behavior across a real store close-and-reopen, not against mocks.
The backend test suite runs green on the pinned toolchain with per-run HANDSHAKE_DATA_DIR isolation and no shared-store contention between binaries.

proof_targets: PT-141-1: repo-wide scan proving zero PG/SQLite language under the backend test tree (tripwire exceptions enumerated).
PT-141-2: full backend test-suite run results on the pinned toolchain, per-binary, with zero failures and a nonzero executed count per binary.
PT-141-3: a disposition table mapping every retired test to its superseding proof.
scope.risk_if_missed: The backend test tree stays permanently red, no backend behavior change can be proven, and forbidden PostgreSQL language survives across ~190 proof files.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend test-harness port with no operator-visible surface.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Pure test-harness change: no product behavior, tool, command, IPC channel, config key, or navigation path changes.

risks: Deleting failing tests instead of porting them silently removes proof coverage across the whole backend (AC-141-2's disposition table exists to catch this).
In-memory or mock stores would make durability tests tautological; AC-141-3 requires real close-and-reopen.
A bulk mechanical port can invert assertion polarity or drop negative-path checks unnoticed.
minimum_controls: Every ported durability proof touches a real embedded SurrealDB store, never a mock.
Every retirement names its superseding proof in PT-141-3.
Suite results must show a nonzero executed count per binary so 0-test greens are never counted as coverage.

hbr_obligations.INT: HBR-INT-009: Flight Recorder NOT_APPLICABLE (test-harness port); internal_diagnostics and Palmistry DEFERRED-with-reason while unshipped per CX-981-005.
hbr_obligations.STOP: The suite may not be made green by narrowing, ignoring, or deleting assertions; closures are ports, equivalently-strong replacements, or typed retirements with named successors.
